sources.title: Marihuana Tax Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 551

supportedFacts: Titre officiel Marihuana Tax Act of 1937 et date du 2 août 1937.
Taxe spéciale et règles de transfert.
La définition excluait notamment les tiges mûres, les fibres correspondantes et certains produits de graines.

sources.title: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Rescheduling of Marijuana
sources.author: Drug Enforcement Administration
sources.passage: Federal History of Marijuana Control; discussion of CSA enactment
sources.limitation: Notice rétrospective institutionnelle consultée pour le fait de classement initial; les questions évitent d’extrapoler les motivations historiques.
supportedFacts: Le CSA a été adopté en 1970.
Le Congrès a initialement placé la marijuana en Schedule I.
Le CSA comporte cinq schedules.

sources.title: Hemp For Victory, circa 1942
sources.organization: USDA National Agricultural Library Special Collections
sources.author: United States Department of Agriculture

sources.limitation: Notice de catalogue, datation approximative; elle n’établit pas à elle seule les détails de toute la campagne de guerre.
supportedFacts: Existence et titre du film Hemp for Victory.
Production attribuée à l’USDA et datation approximative de 1942.

sources.title: Ley N° 19.172: Regulación y control del cannabis
sources.organization: Presidencia de la República Oriental del Uruguay
sources.author: Poder Legislativo / Presidencia de Uruguay
sources.passage: Notice de la loi, date, résumé et lien vers le texte
sources.limitation: Page officielle en espagnol; les dates de promulgation et publication sont distinguées. Ne décrit pas à elle seule les modalités réglementaires actuelles.
supportedFacts: La loi 19.172 est datée du 20 décembre 2013.
Elle confie à l’État le contrôle/régulation de plusieurs activités liées au cannabis.
Ses principes citent santé publique et réduction des risques.

sources.title: Taking stock of progress: Cannabis legalization and regulation in Canada
sources.author: Health Canada
sources.passage: Cannabis Act coming into force; first year and October 2019 product classes
sources.limitation: Bilan officiel de mise en œuvre; ne résume pas toutes les lois provinciales et territoriales.
supportedFacts: La Cannabis Act a reçu la sanction royale le 21 juin 2018.
La loi est entrée en vigueur le 17 octobre 2018.
Comestibles, extraits et produits topiques ont été autorisés sous règles modifiées le 17 octobre 2019.

sources.title: The International Drug Control Conventions
sources.organization: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime / United Nations
sources.author: United Nations

sources.limitation: Compilation des textes conventionnels et repères de conférences; ne constitue pas une interprétation juridique de chaque droit national.
supportedFacts: Convention unique adoptée et ouverte à la signature à New York du 24 janvier au 25 mars 1961; entrée en vigueur en 1964.
Convention sur les substances psychotropes adoptée à Vienne en 1971.
Convention contre le trafic illicite adoptée à Vienne du 25 novembre au 20 décembre 1988.
Convention de 1961 amendée par le protocole de 1972.

sources.title: E/2020/28/Add.1: Report of the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, reconvened 63rd session
sources.organization: United Nations Economic and Social Council
sources.author: Commission on Narcotic Drugs
sources.passage: Decision 63/17; first meeting, paragraph on roll-call vote
sources.limitation: Décision limitée aux annexes de la Convention de 1961. Ne constitue pas une légalisation nationale ou mondiale; cannabis reste dans l’annexe I.
supportedFacts: Vote de 27 pour, 25 contre et une abstention.
Retrait du cannabis et de la résine de l’annexe IV de la Convention unique de 1961.

sources.title: On the Preparations of the Indian Hemp, or Gunjah

supportedFacts: Article sur les préparations de chanvre indien et leurs effets médicaux rapportés.
Évoque le tétanos et d’autres maladies convulsives.
Publication de 1843 consultable en texte intégral.

supportedFacts: Rétrospective historique de la chimie du cannabidiol.

sources.title: Hashish. I. The structure of cannabidiol
sources.author: Raphael Mechoulam and Yehiel Shvo
sources.passage: Tetrahedron 19, 2073–2078 ; page 2073, affiliations et introduction
sources.limitation: Copy of the primary article hosted by a third party; supports the structural research milestone, not clinical efficacy.
supportedFacts: 1963 publication describes CBD structural elucidation and relative stereochemistry.

sources.title: Isolation, Structure, and Partial Synthesis of an Active Constituent of Hashish
sources.organization: Journal of the American Chemical Society / American Chemical Society
sources.author: Yehiel Gaoni and Raphael Mechoulam
sources.passage: JACS 86(8), pp. 1646–1647 ; titre et métadonnées éditoriales
sources.limitation: Institutional article landing page; full article is paywalled. Supports article identity and reported isolation/structure/partial synthesis, not clinical claims.
supportedFacts: Article reports isolation, structural work and partial synthesis of an active hashish constituent, Δ9-THC.
Authors affiliated with Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel.

sources.title: Cannabinoid Receptors: Nomenclature and Pharmacological Principles
sources.organization: Progress in Neuro-Psychopharmacology & Biological Psychiatry / PubMed Central
sources.author: Linda Console-Bram, Jahan Marcu et Mary E. Abood
sources.passage: Historical overview and receptor nomenclature
sources.limitation: Review of the receptor field, rather than the original 1988 binding paper.
supportedFacts: A cannabinoid binding site/receptor was reported in 1988.
CB1 was cloned in 1990.

sources.title: Structure of a cannabinoid receptor and functional expression of the cloned cDNA
sources.author: L. A. Matsuda et al.
sources.passage: Abstract
sources.limitation: PubMed abstract consulted; details beyond abstract and full experimental data are not claimed.
supportedFacts: Matsuda and colleagues reported cloning and expression of CB1.
Abstract reports receptor mRNA in brain regions and cell lines.

sources.title: Molecular characterization of a peripheral receptor for cannabinoids
sources.author: S. Munro, K. L. Thomas, M. Abu-Shaar
sources.passage: Abstract
sources.limitation: PubMed abstract consulted. Initial splenic localization does not establish exclusive tissue distribution.
supportedFacts: Paper reports cloning of a cannabinoid receptor outside brain, in splenic marginal-zone macrophages.
The receptor became known as CB2.

sources.title: Isolation and structure of a brain constituent that binds to the cannabinoid receptor
sources.author: W. A. Devane et al.
sources.passage: Abstract
sources.limitation: PubMed abstract consulted; statements restricted to isolation, receptor binding and proposed endogenous-ligand role.
supportedFacts: Anandamide (N-arachidonoylethanolamine) isolated from porcine brain.
Authors proposed it may function as a natural ligand for cannabinoid receptor.
Name derives from Sanskrit term for bliss.

sources.title: 2-Arachidonoylglycerol: a possible endogenous cannabinoid receptor ligand in brain
sources.organization: Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications / PubMed
sources.author: T. Sugiura et al.
sources.passage: Abstract
sources.limitation: PubMed abstract only; first paper frames 2-AG as a possible ligand based on binding assays, not a complete account of physiological roles.
supportedFacts: 2-AG binding assessed by competition with radiolabeled ligand at synaptosomal membranes.
Authors concluded 2-AG may be an endogenous cannabinoid receptor ligand.
2-AG is 2-arachidonoylglycerol, a monoacylglycerol.

sources.title: International Union of Pharmacology. XXVII. Classification of cannabinoid receptors
sources.author: A. C. Howlett et al.
sources.passage: Abstract
sources.limitation: Review abstract; broad receptor descriptions, not a primary experiment. Tissue distributions are described as predominant rather than exclusive.
supportedFacts: CB1 cloned 1990 and CB2 cloned 1993.
CB1 and CB2 are GPCRs with about 48 percent amino-acid sequence identity.
Receptor signaling can modulate adenylyl cyclase and neurotransmitter release.

sources.title: Proposition 215: Text of Proposed Law
sources.author: California voters / Secretary of State archive
sources.passage: Proposition 215; Section 11362.5, Compassionate Use Act of 1996
sources.limitation: Historical text of this California state initiative; does not establish federal law or present-day law in other jurisdictions.
supportedFacts: California Proposition 215 is also titled the Compassionate Use Act of 1996.
It was placed in the 5 November 1996 election.

sources.title: Congressional Record: National Commission on Marihuana and Drug Abuse report
sources.author: U.S. House of Representatives; report by National Commission on Marihuana and Drug Abuse
sources.passage: Congressional Record, House, report summary; report title and commission presentation
sources.limitation: Contemporary Congressional Record summary of the commission report; used for its title, date, chair and described recommendations.
supportedFacts: The report was titled Marihuana: A Signal of Misunderstanding.
It was presented on 22 March 1972 by the National Commission on Marihuana and Drug Abuse, chaired by Raymond P. Shafer.

supportedFacts: The report is titled The Marihuana Problem in the City of New York and dates to 1944.
The New York Academy of Medicine supervised the sociological study; the Research Council of the Department of Hospitals supervised the clinical study.

sources.title: Narcotics Enforcement in the 1930s
sources.author: Drug Enforcement Administration Museum
sources.passage: Section ?The New Federal Bureau of Narcotics?
sources.limitation: Institutional historical exhibit; used for appointment and tenure facts, not as evidence of a sole cause of policy.
supportedFacts: The Federal Bureau of Narcotics was founded in 1930.
Harry Anslinger was appointed its first commissioner and led it until 1962.

sources.title: Resolution concerning the Report of the Indian Hemp Drugs Commission
sources.organization: National Library of Scotland, India Office Records digital collection
sources.author: Government of India, Finance and Commerce Department
sources.passage: Resolution paragraphs 1?2 on appointment, remit and inquiry area
sources.limitation: Contemporary colonial government record; reflects the inquiry?s official remit, not a neutral modern evaluation of its conclusions.
supportedFacts: The commission was appointed in 1893 and its report was received in 1894.
Its remit covered cultivation, preparations, trade and effects of hemp drugs across India, not Bengal alone.

sources.title: International Opium Convention, Geneva, 19 February 1925
sources.author: League of Nations; depositary record by United Nations
sources.passage: Treaty title and header, lines 0?8
sources.limitation: The cited deposited text consolidates later amendments; question tests only treaty identity and original Geneva date.

sources.limitation: The article page exposes bibliographic details and abstract; full PDF could not be opened during this review. It is the original article on continuing cannabinol research, not a modern structure determination.
supportedFacts: Wood, Spivey and Easterfield authored the early cannabinol research.
Their paper ?Cannabinol. Part I? appeared in 1899 and refers to earlier work.

sources.title: Molecular characterization of an enzyme that degrades neuromodulatory fatty-acid amides
sources.author: B. F. Cravatt et al.
sources.passage: Abstract
sources.limitation: PubMed abstract consulted; statements are limited to the enzyme and substrate relationships described there.
supportedFacts: Cravatt and colleagues isolated, cloned and expressed the enzyme activity named fatty-acid amide hydrolase (FAAH).
The paper reports FAAH conversion of anandamide to arachidonic acid.

sources.title: Molecular characterization of an enzyme that degrades neuromodulatory fatty-acid amides
sources.author: B. F. Cravatt et al.
sources.passage: Abstract; anandamide hydrolysis products
sources.limitation: PubMed abstract consulted; it reports products of hydrolysis, not all pathways for anandamide metabolism.
supportedFacts: FAAH hydrolyses anandamide to arachidonic acid and ethanolamine.

sources.title: A role for monoglyceride lipase in 2-arachidonoylglycerol inactivation
sources.organization: Chemistry and Physics of Lipids / PubMed
sources.author: Thien P. Dinh, T?mas F. Freund and Daniele Piomelli
sources.passage: Abstract; neuronal cell experiments and conclusion
sources.limitation: PubMed abstract consulted; authors state MGL hydrolysis may be a primary route in intact neurons, not the sole route in every tissue.
supportedFacts: MGL/MAGL overexpression increased degradation of endogenously produced 2-AG in rat cortical neurons.
The reported effect was not observed for anandamide degradation.

sources.title: Cloning of the first sn1-DAG lipases points to the spatial and temporal regulation of endocannabinoid signaling in the brain
sources.organization: Journal of Cell Biology / PubMed Central
sources.author: Tiziana Bisogno et al.
sources.passage: Abstract and Introduction, DAG lipase conversion of DAG to 2-AG
sources.limitation: Experimental study of enzymes and brain signaling; the question uses the biochemical conversion without generalizing every physiological context.
supportedFacts: DAG lipase activity synthesizes 2-AG from diacylglycerol.
The article reports cloning and enzymatic characterization of specific sn-1 DAG lipases.

sources.title: Prenylation of olivetolate by a hemp transferase yields cannabigerolic acid, the precursor of tetrahydrocannabinol
sources.author: M. Fellermeier and M. H. Zenk
sources.passage: Abstract
sources.limitation: PubMed abstract consulted; reports enzymatic activity and precursor formation, not a practical protocol.
supportedFacts: A hemp transferase uses geranylpyrophosphate and olivetolic acid in cannabinoid biosynthesis.
The reaction yields cannabigerolic acid (CBGA), a precursor in the cannabinoid pathway.
